paper_summary: Analytical paper proposing a closed-form model (Benveniste-Miloh equivalent filler + Eshelby/Mori-Tanaka) for the thermal conductivity of syntactic foams with spherical microballoons. It is validated against literature data (Liang & Li, Polym. Test. 2006/2007) for polypropylene filled with silicate hollow microballoons TK35 (35 um, 680 kg/m3, core fraction 0.692) and TK70 (70 um, 210 kg/m3, core fraction 0.905) at microballoon volume fractions up to 0.25, and parametric studies vary volume fraction, relative wall thickness and shell/matrix conductivity ratio.
extraction_notes: No numerical composite property values are reported in text or tables: predicted, experimental and FEA thermal conductivities appear only as normalized curves in Fig. 2 (keff/km vs fmb) and parametric plots in Fig. 3, so no records were created (reading values off the plots is not permitted). Table 1 gives only constituent data (secondary, from Liang & Li refs 16,17): PP matrix k = 0.235 W/mK; shell density 2210 kg/m3, k = 0.17934 W/mK; core (gas) 0.0899 kg/m3, k = 0.0228 W/mK; TK35 microballoon 680 kg/m3, k_mb = 0.06035 W/mK, OD 35 um, ID 30.963 um; TK70 210 kg/m3, k_mb = 0.03364 W/mK, OD 70 um, ID 67.710 um. Core volume fractions 0.692 (TK35) and 0.905 (TK70), i.e. radius ratio eta = 0.885 and 0.967. Any experimental composite data should be sourced from Liang & Li (2006, 2007).
